sources.text: Ensamble Kapicúa es the leading band from the MAU (Movimiento Acústico Urbano in Spanish, Urban Acustic Movement) composed of Alvaro Paiva Bimbo (Cabijazz , Filarmónica Desenredada), Edward Ramírez ( C4 Trío ) and Jorge Torres They started playing around 2001 making new compositions with traditional instruments of Venezuela, influenced beside of the folklore music also by jazz and academic music, leading together with some bands to the MAU. They have released two studio albums "Muscapicúa" (2005) and "Bravedad" (2011) and one live album simply called "En Vivo" (2009). They are currently in Hiatus.

sources.text:
An exceptional venezuelan composer, cuatro and guitar player who earned the Bachelor of Music Degree in Composition from UNEARTE (Experimental University of the Arts) Venezuela. He has shared the stage with very acclaimed musicians.
He is a founder member (2000) of the venezuelan music ensemble “Los Sinvergüenzas”. His work with “Los Sinvergüenzas” has already been included in five recording productions.
In 2010 he won the 2nd Prize at the Composition Competition “José Fernandez Rojas” in Spain, with his work “Suite Latinoamericana” for Plectrum Orchestra.
Héctor belongs to “C4 Trío” (2005) along with Jorge Glem, Edward Ramirez and Rodner Padilla. With C4 Trio he has recorded seven albums and a DVD and has been nominated five times for the Latin Grammys and has won two; in 2014 as "Best Recording Engineering for an Album" for the album "De Repente" and in 2019 as "Best Folkloric Album" for "Tiempo al tiempo". Also with “C4 Trío” he has been nominated twice for the Grammy Awards in 2018 with the album "Pa Fuera" and in 2020 with "Tiempo al tiempo". With “C4 Trío” he maintains an intense concert schedule in the most important theaters and festivals in North, Central, South America and Europe.
In 2018 Héctor release his first album called "Giros", where some of the most important Venezuelan musicians participate and where he shows more of his role as a composer. In 2022 he releases the album "Travesía", an album of Cuatro soloists.

sources.text:
Venezuelan Cuatro player. The Cuatro is a traditional four string Venezuelan instrument used in Venezuelan Folk music. However Jorge Glem and his Cuatro band "C4trio", play other genres with the Cuatro as well. Like Venezuela, other Latin American Countries have the "Cuatro" as a traditional instrument. An example is the Puerto Rican Cuatro; though it has also four strings, the instrument is built differently and even has a different sound.
Jorge is an extremely virtuous Cuatro player, one of the elements that set him apart from other Cuatro players other than his virtuosity, is the fact that he incorporates percussion into his playing by using the surface of the cuatro. He can also play extremely fast and still keep a clean sound.

José Manuel Pinto es un cantautor, productor y sonidista nacido en Caracas y que desde temprana edad mostró grandes inquietudes musicales. Aunque se decanta por el piano como instrumento para su expresión musical, también domina otros instrumentos como la guitarra eléctrica y acústica, el bajo y algunos instrumentos de percusión menor. 
 Formación musical 
 José Manuel Pinto realiza estudios musicales en el Berklee College of Music (Boston, Estados Unidos) y el Taller de Arte Sonoro (Caracas, Venezuela); así como también enseñanzas de piano y armonías con el maestro Gerry Weil. Desarrolla una gran actividad como ingeniero de sonido trabajando con músicos de prestigio como Pablo Gil , Raimundo Rodulfo , Kré y Ricochet . Sin embargo, esa faceta como productor e ingeniero de sonido no le permite plasmar su talento como compositor en obras discográficas. Paralelamente desarrolla actividades orientadas hacía la producción musical, además de una importante labor como docente. Dentro de la labor como docente, publica el libro El Nuevo Cuaderno de Música Para Guitarra «
 Producción musical 
 Como solista,debuta con el álbum Caracas Saudade Tropica l (2007) donde ofrece una fusión de diferentes ritmos con el jazz como elemento protagónico combinado con ritmos como el cool y el bossa nova, del cual extrae el tema Tanto como sencillo. El disco es recibido con gran aceptación dentro de los círculos de jazz y música electroacústica urbana.

sources.text:
Winners of the Pepsi Music Award on their album “Sinvergüensuranzas” as the best traditional instrumental music album of the year 2013, this group from Mérida, Venezuela, has managed to conjugate the creation and the performance of the most representative genres of our musical patrimony. This versatile ensemble has eventually transformed into the inheritors of the musical tradition that institutions such as “El Cuarteto” and “Raíces de Venezuela” imposed, adding a hint of Jazz, a bit of fusion and dressing it with a fair touch of humor which always turns us into accomplices for good taste and good music.

 

Since 1999, the year where the group was founded, Los Sinvergüenzas have been always very clear on what they wanted to achieve in the genre of venezuelan instrumental music. What began as a musical experiment in the city of Mérida (Venezuela), performing a repertoire including the most renowned pieces of our musical patrimony, they have adventured since then, in the composition of a very strict repertoire with traditional roots combined with jazz influences and contemporary music that each of their members handles with great expertise thanks to their years of training as academic musicians.

 

The youth of their members is an asset to their constant evolution and the strong conviction that with their music they will contribute to the development of public conscience, offering competitivity to a national artistic expression next to other acclaimed musical expressions from foreign countries.

 

Los Sinvergüenzas have offered concerts in the most important halls of Venezuela, and they have represented their country in many important international festivals, being welcomed with the enthusiasm and the affection from those who enjoy good music. In the last three years, they have been invited to participate and collaborate in concerts and recordings with the most renowned groups and singers.

 

The ensemble counts with four record productions: “Bichoneando” (2000), “Desde otro Lugar” (2007), “Sinverguensuranzas” (2012) and "Raíces (2013).

 

 

Reviews

 

“Everything has just the right proportions; there isn’t an excessive dose of any element whatsoever and you can appreciate the love and the professionalism while mixing the ingredients, the texture, the color and the variety of flavours,  succeeding to delight the most exquisite palates (or ears).”

 

Raúl Delgado Estévez, El Cuarteto. Caracas, 2006

 

“In a sonorous setting where listening to the same pieces over and over again in a thousand different versions, becomes monotonous, the important contribution from Los Sinvergüenzas gives a breath of fresh air to the traditional instrumental venezuelan music environment.”

 

César Alejandro Carrillo, Conductor of the Orfeón Universitario UCV. Caracas, 2010

 

“… I can assure that they have risen as the inheritors of a generation of instrumental venezuelan music groups, that from a long time ago, have been pointing the road to follow among popular art.”

 

Orlando Moret, Raíces de Venezuela group. Mérida, 2000

 

 “… To listen to Los Sinvergüenzas is always gratifying; In their hands, traditional music impregnates with humor and transforms, without a doubt, into modernity.”

Papel Literario, El Nacional. Caracas, 2009

 

 

“…A production firmly transiting towards the rejuvenation of a musical characterization in Venezuela: what these people do will transcend, without any […]

sources.text: Los Sinvergüenzas, musical ensemble, was born as a music experiment in Mérida, Venezuela in 1999. Its musicians created a compilation of the folk music, and then they made some adaptations to the new style of interpretations. Later, in February 2000, they founded this ensemble with a concert which took place in the Aula Magna of the University of Los Andes; since then, they have made an important work when it comes to compositions and musical arrangements of the Venezuelan folk music genre. The youth of its integrants allows a work in a continuous evolution. This particularity gives them a chance to get involved into de vast musical ensembles movement. They don’t want to continue with the 50 years ago interpretation style; on the contrary, they seek to improve their interpretation and produce a new style of the Venezuelan folk music. Among the arrangements, there is a large diversity that has always distinguished the Venezuelan music (Jazz + folkloric music + academic music), this is a result of the different music tendencies of each member of the group. They don’t attempt to be the pioneers nor the best interpreters of this music, on the contrary, they just would like to cultivate a conscience of the Venezuelan folk music in an international level. This young musicians want to create a prestige of this new artistic expression, and achieve the same artistic level as the respected and famous foreign music that, in one way or another, has influenced this new tendency of the Venezuelan folk music. Los Sinvergüenzas ensemble has had an excellent acceptance not only by the Venezuelan public, but also by the international public. They have had also the honor of represent Venezuela in different music festivals, receiving outstanding comments.

sources.text: PABELLÓN SIN BARANDA ha sido considerado en su país de origen, Venezuela, una de las agrupaciones punteras en la vanguardia musical. Desde sus inicios en 1993 ellos han cultivado una visión estética “sin Barandas”, es decir, sin límites. Su música está arraigada en lo folklórico y tradicional de Venezuela, y la fusionan con sabores musicales de otras culturas. En 1997 PABELLÓN SIN BARANDA fue nominado al premio Casa del Artista (Venezuela). PABELLÓN SIN BARANDA ha compartido escenario con figuras nacionales como El Cuarteto, Saúl Vera, Serenata Guayanesa, Orquesta Nacional de Flautas, e internacionales de la talla de Tania Libertad, Tango Emoción, Irakere e Iván Lins. ¿Qué significa Pabellón?: Este es un plato de comida típico de Venezuela, en el cual se combina la carne mechada (carne de res deshebrada), el arroz, las caraotas (frijoles negros) y el plátano en rebanadas, o “tajadas”, como le decimos en Venezuela. Estas tajadas son llamadas coloquialmente “barandas”, o rejas, por estar ubicadas de los lados del plato donde se sirve el resto del pabellón. Orlando Cardozo, cuatro Orlando es ejecutante de cuatro, clarinete y mandolina. Obtuvo una licenciatura en composición, Cum Laude, en el Instituto Universitario de Estudios Musicales (Caracas). Además ha realizado estudios de música popular en los Talleres de la Fundación Bigott, Armonía e Improvisación Aplicada al Jazz con Gerry Weill y Armonía en la Música Popular con Carmelo Rodríguez. Como compositor y arreglista ha producido obras en los géneros popular, de cámara, sinfónico, coral, solista y electroacústico. Orlando fue ganador del Segundo Premio en el Primer Salón Nacional de Jóvenes Compositores por su poema sinfónico “El Crepúsculo del Diablo”. Orlando está a cargo de la Cátedra de Música de Cámara Venezolana en el Instituto Universitario de Estudios Musicales y de las cátedras de armonía y composición de la Escuela de Música “José Reyna”. Y es miembro de las agrupaciones “Ensamble Catako”, “Ensamble Morichal” y “Grupo Atrio”, en calidad de instrumentista, compositor y arreglista. Pedro Vásquez, violoncello Pedro ha participado en grupos diversos como “Alzheimer”, con Paul Desenne y Alonso Toro, “Tuyero Submarín” y las orquestas “Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho”, Jóvenes Arcos y Cámara Venezuela. Sus profesores de violoncello fueron William Molina y Paul Dessene y realizó cursos con Philippe Muller, Frans Helmerson y Janos Starker. También ha incursionado en la composición. Entre sus profesores se cuentan Blas Atehortúa y Leo Broker. Pedro ha compuesto música para teatro, performance, y adelantos en una nueva actitud para la canción popular, así como encargos para agrupaciones de música de cámara. Como docente se ha desempeñado en los diversos núcleos del Sistema Nacional de Orquestas Juveniles e Infantiles de Venezuela. Pedro es locutor y productor de los programas radiales “América Latina: Territorio Pop” y “Planeta Cangrejo” que se transmiten en la Radio Nacional de Venezuela. Javier Montilla, flauta Javier se formó en el Sistema Nacional de Orquestas Juveniles e Infantiles de Venezuela. Sus profesores de flauta han sido Víctor Rojas, José Antonio Naranjo, Glenn Egner, Alexa Still y John Bailey. Javier posee una licenciatura, una maestría y un doctorado en ejecución de la flauta de las siguientes instituciones, respectivamente: Instituto Universitario de Estudios Musicales (Caracas), Universidad de Colorado en Boulder y la Universidad de Nebraska en Lincoln.
